newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-No cut in Swedish repo rate this week.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-No cut in Swedish repo rate this week.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, is not expected to change its key interest rate, the repo rate, at its weekly tender operation on Tuesday, a Reuters poll of 12 economists found on Monday.
Economists said a weak crown was continuing to hinder, and the repo would be left at its current rate of 4.10 percent at the 0830 GMT tender.
"We don't think there will be any changes in the repo rate on Tuesday as the crown has not strengthened sufficiently," said Magnus Matstoms of Carnegie.
"We have worked out a model that shows that since the crown was floated in November 1992 developments in inflation can be explained by about 80 percent of the variation in the value of the crown.
"Therefore the crown should be important in the Riksbank's estimates."
Many economists also pointed out there has been no significant data since the Riksbank last refrained from cutting the rate.
Some said the central bank could be waiting to see the latest Consumer Price Index for January on February 20 before making any move.
But economists said there was still room for a cut.
Continuing low inflation was supporting another cut in the repo rate which is the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
"I think that there is some reason to lower now but I don't think they will. The picture of the Swedish economy seems good and inflation is low," said Thomas Lindberg of Ohman Fondkommission.

Economists interviewed for the poll were from Aragon, Carnegie, Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, IDEA, Salomon Brothers, Swedbank, UBS, Unibank, and Ohmans Fondkommission.
The repo rate was last cut on December 17.
